name: PLA (Polylactic Acid)
chemical_makeup: Polylactic acid, a biodegradable aliphatic polyester derived from fermented plant starch
summary: The default FDM material: easiest to print, stiff, accurate, inexpensive — but soft above ~55 °C and brittle under impact. Example entry pending Phase A research.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping/steam at nozzle; clean glossy extrudate; minimal stringing on retraction test

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant between uses; tolerates weeks of open air in dry climates

not_recommended: parts in hot cars or sun

compatibility.notes: PETG and PLA separate cleanly, so each works as a support interface for the other

plate_recommendations.notes: No adhesive needed on a clean plate

emissions.notes: Lowest-emission common filament; sweet odor is lactide. Ventilation still sensible for continuous printing in occupied rooms.

safety_notes: Additive-heavy variants (glow, metal-filled) change the emission and abrasion picture — see variation entries

sources: EXAMPLE ENTRY — values are typical published figures; replace via Phase A research
